prerequisites: A prior knowledge of solid materials and their properties, including different classes of materials (metals, polymers, ceramics, etc.) and fundamental principles of materials science.

A solid foundation in general mechanics, particularly regarding concepts of forces, stresses, deformations, and laws of material strength. Students must be able to analyze the mechanical behaviors of materials under different loading conditions.

A good understanding of thermal principles is necessary to address the thermomechanical aspects of the course, such as the thermal behavior of ceramics, creep, and thermal shocks. This includes basic knowledge in thermodynamics, heat transfer, and high-temperature material behavior.

learning_outcomes.text: Master the properties of ceramics, especially their physical and mechanical characteristics.
Understand the different types of ceramics (traditional, technical, and thermomechanical) and their industrial applications.
Know the manufacturing techniques for ceramics, especially sintering and its mechanisms.
Understand the origin of ceramic fragility and how they behave under stress.
Grasp the notion of toughness and its importance for ceramic performance.
Be able to calculate the probability of rupture of a ceramic part using statistical models, such as the Weibull model.
Be able to predict the lifespan of a ceramic part from SPT diagrams and proof tests.

Be able to identify and analyze the different degradation mechanisms of ceramics, such as rupture (brittle fracture and delayed fracture), static fatigue and subcritical cracking, creep (viscous, diffusional, cavitation creep), thermal shocks and their impacts on material resistance.
Apply the studied concepts to understand and predict the behavior of ceramics under various operating conditions.
Be able to analyze and interpret tests and experimental data related to ceramics.

syllabus_topics: Structure & microstructure: Constituents, Crystallography, Temperature transformations
Mechanical behavior: Mechanical properties, Mechanical characterization
Ceramic fatigue: Subcritical cracking, Lifespan estimation
Thermomechanical behavior: Thermal shocks, Ceramic creep
teaching_methods: Detailed theoretical lectures on ceramic properties, manufacturing methods, degradation and damage mechanisms, including key concepts like fragility, toughness, rupture, fatigue, creep, and thermal shocks with practical examples.
Practical case studies illustrating industrial applications of ceramics, especially in thermomechanical performance-critical sectors, highlighting real challenges and possible solutions.
Exercises and practical calculations on rupture probability and lifespan prediction using statistical models (Weibull model) and SPT diagrams.

Experimental demonstrations or simulations of tests (rupture, fatigue, creep, thermal shock) to understand phenomena and their impact on ceramic materials, comparing experimental results with theoretical models.
Tutorials (TD) for group work on specific problems, calculations, analyses, and discussion of results.
Seminars and conferences with specialists and professionals from the thermomechanical ceramics sector to provide practical and current industry perspectives.
assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is 1*DS1/1. Students must prepare for tutorials and practical work by reading provided documents and familiarizing themselves with theoretical concepts.
degree: Titre d'ingénieur ENIT (cycle ingénieur, semestres 5-10; orientación mecánica/producción)
